Bianca Goodson Trillian

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A fascinating look inside the web of corruption that is the Gupta empire with an exclusive interview with Bianca Goodson

Unique Selling Point:
We have filmed an excellent interview with former Trillian Management Consulting CEO Bianca Goodson. Trillian and international consulting giant McKinsey have been implicated in multi-billion rand corrupt deals with several SOE's. Bianca bore witness to the corruption, and offers an insider's view of the Gupta way of doing business.

Summary:
Bianca has testified in parliament and supplied a written affidavit to then Public Protector Thuli Madonsela. She witnessed the inner dealings of what turned out to be a Gupta front company for siphoning off billions from state owned enterprises. Trillian facilitated access to decision makers for consulting multinationals McKinsey and Oliver Wyman. In return for the political connections, Bianca says Trillian was to get up to half the consulting fees in lucrative consulting contracts with state entities. This effectively meant where Trillian was only supposed to be the the local development partner in these contracts, they were actually calling the shots, deciding who could get the government contracts through their connections to government.

Press Release:



Trillian: Bianca Goodson Speaks
In an in-depth interview, former Trillian executive, Bianca Goodson lifts the lid on the inner workings of the Gupta empire, revealing how Gupta-linked companies planned to siphon billions from State-owned enterprises. Goodson also opens up to Carte Blanche about the secret life of a whistle-blower – the fear, anxiety and depression associated with speaking up.


Script:


Bianca Goodson
24 January 2017

Voice
In September 2016 a young executive, unknown to the public at large, received a phone call from then Public Protector Thuli Madonsela’s offices. The Public Protector wanted to know about her involvement in Trillian Management Consultants, a subsidiary of Trillian Capital Partners, the company in which Gupta confidant Salim Essa owned 60% of the shares.

Sound Up Bianca Goodson
Bianca: Up until that point I suspected that things weren’t cool with Trillion, I couldn’t prove it. And then Thuli phoned me and it was like ok things just got real.

Macfarlane: No one just gets a call from the public protector…

Bianca: She wouldn’t be calling me if things were cool right?

Link Macfarlane
Bianca Goodson, a senior executive at Trillion, was one of the original whistleblowers who opened a can of worms, exposing billions of rands of suspect dealings between Gupta linked companies and state owned enterprises.

Voice
Goodson’s story starts in November 2015, when Clive Angel from Integrated Capital Management offered the former mining executive a position at the brand new Trillian Management Consultants.

Sound Up Bianca
And when Clive explained their role in the whole thing they said that they were appointed by Salim to be the IPO. They were appointed to setup Trillian.

Voice
Goodson was told that Trillian would be doing consulting work for Eskom, ostensibly to turn around the struggling power utility. From the get go Trillian’s luck seemed too good to be true. Although they were only a start up company at the time, Trillian, together with US based consulting giant Mckinsey,]had secured a R475 million rand down payment from Eskom for a project called “Top Engineers”. But that was only the beginning.

Sound Up Bianca
Shortly after I signed my employment contract and it was formal that I was on board and I was a director, the first Excel spreadsheets with the cash flows were shared to me from Mckinsey. And that indicated R10 billion over three years. I fell over in my chair. In my mind nobody gets that lucky.

Voice
According to Goodson that wasn’t the end of Trillian’s good fortunes. Salim Essa had managed to secure Trillian 50% of the revenues, not bad for the South African start up who was supposed to be the junior supplier development partner to Mckinsey.

Sound Up Bianca
Macfarlane: What did Trillian get in return?

Bianca: Over the entire scope, Trillian got 50%. Salim even made a statement to me very clearly, he said I don’t care what they do, I want my R5 billion. Trillion got half. We had no people doing the work. I was busy employing people.

Link Macfarlane
In the Eskom deal, Trillian was only supposed to be the enterprise development partner. Instead, they became the gatekeepers to the politically connected elite.


Voice
Susan Comrie, an Investigative journalist from Amabhungane spent months researching the Gupta Leaks. She says Salim Essa plays an integral part in the Gupta family’s business dealings

Sound Up Susan Comrie
He’s so integrated into the empire that he’s often referred to as the fourth brother. I mean that’s how close he is. You can’t really separate Salim Essa’s business interests from the Gupta’s business interests. They go hand in hand.

Voice
Essa and the Gupta’s have been fingered in billions of rands of kickback deals at Transnet for the procurement of locomotives - and some of their friends at Transnet eventually moved to Eskom

Sound Up Susan
Now we know that the Gupta’s were already using a huge amount of influence at Transnet when Brian Molefe and Anoj Singh were at Transnet. When the two of them moved across to Eskom, the Guptas started to focus their attention onto Eskom and onto projects there. And looking at how they could extract huge value.

Voice
Goodson says it was Essa who was calling the shots at Eskom during the 5 months that she was employed at Trillion.

Sound Up Bianca
To walk into Salim’s office and you’ve got executive members just chilling in the waiting area, I didn’t see that for the numerous times that I went to the Mckinsey offices.

Voice
Gideon Pogrund is the director of the Gordon Institute of Business Science Ethics and Governance Think Tank. He compares unethical behaviour to a virus that spreads from person to person.

Sound Up Gideon
I think that certain parts of our society have been infected with this unethical virus. The good news though is that just like an unethical virus is a threat, ethical behaviour is an opportunity. Just like unethical behaviour spreads, so does ethical behaviour.

Voice
And that’s why he believes the role of whistle blowers cannot be underestimated.

Sound Up Gideon
A Polish diplomat who defected under communism once said that in a room where people unanimously maintain a conspiracy of silence, one word of truth sounds like a pistol shot. In a boardroom or some other corporate setting, that pistol shot can galvanise and encourage others to dissent.

Voice
In hindsight Goodson says there were many red flags raised at Trillion, from small things like people using their personal email addresses:

Sound Up Bianca
Nobody had professional domains, Trillion rolled with Gmail account domain names.

Voice
To much more sinister events.

Sound Up Bianca
I did find it odd that Mohamed Bobat had interviewed me, initially.



Voice
Mohammed Bobat was one of the mystery advisors to Des van Rooyen who was parachuted into National Treasury in December 2015 when President Zuma abruptly fired then Finance Minister Nhlanhla Nene and replaced him with van Rooyen

Sound Up Bianca
And I asked Clive why, and Clive made it very clear to me and he said well if you don’t work out for us Mohammed is going to take your job.
Voice
And Goodson says she knew about the appointment of van Rooyen and Bobat before President Zuma made the announcement public.

Sound Up Bianca
Clive phoned me that morning, to tell me that Mohammed was the special advisor to the minister in treasury.

Voice
The phone call implied that Salim Essa had been busy behind the scenes.

Sound Up Bianca
And he said remember that I told you our boss looks after loyal people.

Voice
Dr. Reuel Khoza is a distinguished businessman, thought leader and President of the Institute of Directors in South Africa. He says whistle blowers face real risks when going public.

Sound Up Dr Reuel Khoza
Whistle blowers are courageous people, because the powers that be, if they got to know about them and they did not have the requisite protection, they could perish career wise. And that actually means even perishing physically, because if your livelihood is interfered with by an evil force, you might wind up even battling to look after your own family.

Voice
He says the succession of scandals we’ve had in our SOE’s speaks to a much greater problem, an institutionalised rot.

Sound Up Reuel
Mac: How dangerous is this for us as a country, how are we looked at internationally as a result of this?

Reuel: Very dangerous indeed, which is why we find ourselves where we are. Where the rot is almost pervasive. It’s manifest in levels of unemployment, particularly amongst the youth, it’s manifest in the lack of growth. Public sector institutions falling like dominoes, falling from the rot. Because if things are rotten, they can’t stand.

Voice
Goodson says the final straw came when Trillian, without any explanation, wanted her to open a another account for the company with India based Bank of Baroda. She says Trillian wanted her to give Marc Chipkin, also an Integrated Capital director, sole authority over the account.

Sound Up Bianca
This guy from the Bank of Baroda says you’ve got to sign this so I say I’m not signing it. I said I need this letter altered. I said this letter will be altered so that Marc Chipkin and I jointly will authorise transactions. Jointly. It was and.

.
Voice
Driving home, Goodson was furious

Sound Up Bianca
To me there was nothing more blatantly obvious how much I was being used then that specific day. That stung so much.

Voice
Goodson handed in her resignation the very next day. Despite initially denying it, Eskom paid Trillion and Mckinsey R1.6 Billion before they pulled the plug on the project.

Sound Up Susan
The sort of tragic thing that you see when you look at those forensic reports, is that you see how mid - level and low- level people in Eskom were bullied into forcing through these payments.

Voice
Life isn’t easy for whistleblowers, especially since they don’t usually get to be in that position without having been in the thick of things.

Mac: So what have you been doing to cope with all of this because this must be a horrible ordeal for anyone to go through.

Bianca: So I think after the third or fourth time of contemplating suicide, I decided that I was just going to pray.

Voice
She says it was ultimately her faith that gave her the strength keep going.

Sound Up Bianca
And lawyers were telling me what not to do and I was like you know what, if something happened and I died and I went straight to heaven I would be so much happier, let just be clear. Because I would be with my father. And I know my parents don’t want to hear this but that’s the trade off that you’ve go to make. And I don’t want my daughter to hear this but I got to the point where dying was easier. So I trust God, and I’ve survived this because he’s been with me.

Voice
In a written response to Carte Blanche Marc Chipkin and Clive Angel deny the allegations against them. Marc DENIES HE WAS MEANT TO BE THE SOLE SIGNATORY ON THE TRILLIAN ACCOUNT AT THE BANK OF BARODA AND says he was given authority by Goodson to open the account. Clive Angel says his only involvement in the Eskom Project was to recruit qualified heads of a team of consulting professionals to work alongside Mckinsey. He also says “ I emphatically deny that I knew beforehand about the appointment of Mr van Rooyen as Minister of Finance. Mohammed Bobat declined an interview on advice from his lawyer, and no one else responded to our requests for comment.

Sound Up Bianca
I did stick to my guns in tho think at regard, that when things looked a bit to shady I would leave, and I did leave. But now personally I still think I was there for three months too long.

Voice
On thursday President Zuma released the terms of reference for the State Capture Commission’s enquiry, but Goodson, who has since her resignation testified in parliament, isn’t expecting things to change anytime soon.

Sound Up Bianca
I hope that the culprits who do this learn that they won’t get away with it. If they get away with it now, or even if they’ve gotten away with it now, if all this money has gone off shore and can’t be clawed back, but these people don’t come back and do it again, I count that as a win. But I’m not necessarily hopeful that their would be rash implications now. I think that may be naive.

metadata.Summary: Bianca has testified in parliament and supplied a written affidavit to then Public Protector Thuli Madonsela. Trillian facilitated access to decision makers for consulting multinationals McKinsey and Oliver Wyman. In return for the political connections, Bianca says Trillian was to get up to half the consulting fees in lucrative consulting contracts with state entities. This effectively meant where Trillian was only supposed to be the the local development partner in these contracts, they were actually calling the shots, deciding who could get the government contracts through their connections to government.
